facts.claim: The law on marriage is the same throughout Italy, but local town halls may interpret it in slightly different ways and waive certain requirements; couples should contact the Registrar's Office of the town hall where they will marry for a definitive document list and submission timing.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy?
facts.use_note: Page modified 22 Oct 2026. Use in H2 1 for the 'confirm with your comune' line.

facts.claim: Documents a US citizen may need: valid US passport (active duty military may use military ID), birth certificate (original or certified copy), and evidence of termination of any previous marriage (final divorce decree, annulment decree or death certificate of former spouse).
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy?
facts.use_note: Documents table. The Embassy labels these 'You may need'; the comune sets the final list.

facts.claim: A woman whose previous marriage ended within the last 300 days must obtain a waiver from the Procura della Repubblica at the court in the city where the new marriage will take place, issued on medical evidence that she is not pregnant.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy?
facts.use_note: Documents section, previously married note.

facts.claim: Americans swear an affidavit called the 'Dichiarazione Giurata' before a US consular officer accredited in Italy, stating there is no legal impediment to the marriage under the laws of the US state where they reside. It is booked as a notary appointment at the Embassy in Rome or the Consulates General in Milan, Florence or Naples (online), or by contacting the Consular Agents in Genoa, Venice or Palermo. The form should be completed in advance but signed only in front of the consular officer.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy?
facts.use_note: The Embassy's own per-post PDFs are titled 'MarriageNullaOsta' and the Florence and Rome district pages say 'notarial appointment to perform the Nulla Osta', so it is accurate to say Italian offices and the Embassy itself treat the Dichiarazione Giurata as the Nulla Osta for Americans. The US does not issue a separate Nulla Osta certificate.

facts.claim: After it is issued, the Dichiarazione Giurata must be legalized at the Legalization Office (Ufficio Legalizzazioni) of a Prefettura, generally within the same consular district where it was executed, with a EUR 16 revenue stamp (marca da bollo) bought at a tabacchi for each document.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy?
facts.use_note: Wedding-week sequence and fee table.

facts.claim: The Atto Notorio is a separate declaration, sworn by two witnesses (any nationality, over 18, valid photo ID, who know the applicant, and who are not family members, future family members or in-laws), that there is no obstacle to the marriage under US law. It can be done before an Italian consul outside Italy or before a court official in Italy. The Embassy advises getting it at the nearest Italian Embassy or Consulate before leaving the US, as some Italian courts have long waiting lists.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy?
facts.use_note: Step-by-step H2. Note 'not family members' is stricter than the ceremony witness rule (F-10).

facts.claim: Atto Notorio in Italy: book in advance with the Ufficio Atti Notori of the court (tribunale ordinario) with jurisdiction over the wedding town, or any other Italian court. An interpreter is required if the applicant or any witness does not speak Italian, and everyone must show proof of legal presence in Italy (for example a plane ticket). Stamps: two of EUR 16 and one of EUR 10.62, ready in about 4 to 10 days; urgent same-day: two of EUR 16 and one of EUR 31.86.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy?
facts.use_note: Totals: standard EUR 42.62, urgent EUR 63.86 (arithmetic from the published stamps). Fee table.

facts.claim: All documents are presented to the Marriage Office (Ufficio Matrimoni) of the town hall where the marriage will take place, where the couple makes a Declaration of Intention to Marry before a civil registrar, with an interpreter if they do not speak Italian. Only then can the date be set.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy?
facts.use_note: Wedding-week sequence. Note the Embassy says the date is set after the declaration; in practice venues hold dates earlier, so say the date is formally fixed by the comune.

facts.claim: Banns are normally posted for two consecutive weeks including two Sundays after the Declaration of Intention, but if neither party is an Italian citizen or resident they are automatically waived or posted for a shorter period (one day to a week, depending on the town hall).
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy?
facts.use_note: Days-needed-in-Italy FAQ.

facts.claim: A civil ceremony is performed by the mayor or a deputy. Two witnesses (any nationality, over 18, valid photo ID) and, if needed, an interpreter must be present; a witness cannot serve as interpreter. Marriage hall rental ranges from EUR 500 to EUR 9,200 depending on location, season and day.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy?
facts.use_note: Ceremony witnesses (unlike Atto Notorio witnesses) are not barred from being relatives on this page, so parents or siblings can witness the ceremony but not the Atto Notorio. Confirm with the comune.

facts.claim: Under Italian law, public documents issued outside the EU are valid for only six months from the date of issue, so documents submitted to Italian authorities should not be issued more than six months before the marriage.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy?
facts.use_note: Core constraint for the backward timeline. Pair with F-19 and F-21 (Atto Notorio three-month / 90-day window), which is tighter.

facts.claim: All documents originating outside Italy must be legalized and translated into Italian. A US document is legalized with an Apostille from the secretary of state of the state where it was issued (Hague Convention). US federal documents get an Apostille from the US Department of State Office of Authentications.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Notarials (Documents Requiring Hague Apostille)
facts.use_note: Main page it.usembassy.gov/getting-married-in-italy/ says the same for state documents. Federal route (e.g. naturalization certificate) is linked from the notarials page; process and fee to be confirmed (see F-24).

facts.claim: The US consular notarial fee is USD 50 per notary seal, paid on the day of the appointment. At the Embassy in Rome payment is by debit or credit card through the government's website (in-person cashier payments suspended); at Milan, Florence and Naples payment is accepted at the consular cashier. Notarials are by appointment only.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Notarials
facts.use_note: Confirms the AI Overview's USD 50. It is per seal: the page says 'With the exception of the Nulla Osta for marriages... a U.S. notary has no affect in Italy', confirming the Nulla Osta is a notarial act. Each partner swears their own Dichiarazione Giurata, so expect USD 50 each (inference: confirm per post). Page modified 28 Aug 2026.

facts.claim: US consular staff cannot translate documents, certify translations, explain document contents, act as witnesses or give legal advice. US consular officers are not trained in Italian law; for detail, consult an Italian consular officer in the US, the town hall civil registrar, or a lawyer licensed in Italy.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy? and Notarials
facts.use_note: Help section. Translation and witness points are on https://it.usembassy.gov/services/notarials/.

facts.claim: US consular districts in Italy: Embassy Rome covers Lazio, Marche, Umbria, Abruzzo and Sardinia; Consulate General Florence covers Tuscany, Emilia-Romagna (except Piacenza and Parma) and San Marino; Consulate General Milan covers Valle d'Aosta, Piemonte, Lombardia, Veneto, Trentino-Alto Adige, Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Liguria and the Piacenza and Parma provinces; Consulate General Naples covers Campania, Molise, Basilicata, Puglia, Calabria and Sicily.
facts.source_name: U.S. Department of State, Italy Judicial Assistance Information
facts.use_note: Page shows 'last updated' 15 Nov 2013, so medium. Consistent with the current it.usembassy.gov district pages (Venice and Genoa agencies sit under Milan; Palermo agency and Salerno Prefettura for the Amalfi Coast under Naples). Region table: Lake Como (Lombardy) = Milan; Tuscany = Florence; Rome = Embassy Rome; Amalfi Coast (Campania) = Naples; Puglia = Naples; Sicily = Naples or Palermo agency; Venice = Milan district, Venice agency. Wedded Advisor to confirm current boundaries.

facts.claim: District specifics: Florence: Dichiarazione at the Consulate General Florence, legalized at the Florence Prefettura (Ufficio Legalizzazione, Mon to Fri 9 to 11 am). Milan: a Dichiarazione from the Milan Consulate can be legalized at any Prefettura in Milan's jurisdiction, but one from the Venice or Genoa consular agencies must be legalized at the Venice or Genoa Prefettura (Milan Prefettura by appointment only). Naples: legalize at the Naples or Palermo Prefettura; couples marrying on the Amalfi Coast may use the Salerno Prefettura to do it the same day. Rome: Embassy Rome, then the Rome Prefettura (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 9 am to 12 pm).
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, consular district marriage pages (Florence, Milan, Naples, Rome)
facts.use_note: Other pages: https://it.usembassy.gov/getting-married-in-the-consular-district-of-florence/ (modified 2025-12), https://it.usembassy.gov/getting-married-in-the-consular-district-of-naples/ (2026-01), https://it.usembassy.gov/getting-married-in-the-consular-district-of-rome/ (2026-04). Office hours change: present as 'limited weekday morning hours', not exact times.

facts.claim: The Naples district page says that generally, couples marrying on the Amalfi Coast do not need the Atto Notorio, and should check with the specific town hall.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in the Consular District of Naples
facts.use_note: Good illustration of comune variation. Say 'some Amalfi Coast town halls have not required it, per the US Embassy; confirm with yours'.

facts.claim: Marriage hall rental by city, per the US Embassy district pages: Florence EUR 750 to EUR 5,000; Milan EUR 500 to EUR 596; Venice EUR 1,600 to EUR 9,200; Genoa EUR 25 to EUR 1,500; Rome EUR 1,392 to EUR 1,624 (most Rome civil weddings are at the Complesso di Vignola Mattei, and on weekends also at the Campidoglio); Palermo: no rental fee. Fees vary by season and day of week.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, consular district marriage pages
facts.use_note: City-hall figures only; private venues and other comuni set their own fees. Some district pages were last modified Dec 2025, so figures may be dated; tell readers to confirm with the comune. Sources: Florence, Milan (Milan, Venice, Genoa), Rome and Naples (Palermo) district pages.

facts.claim: The Italian Consulate General in New York requires, for US citizens marrying in Italy, an Atto Notorio sworn by four witnesses (over 18, unrelated to either party or to each other) who appear in person with a valid ID (passport) before the Italian consular officer with jurisdiction over the applicant's place of residence. It must be executed within three months of the marriage date. Requests go by email with the application form to the Legal Office (newyork.notarile@esteri.it); appointments are made online via Prenot@mi.
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia a New York, Atto Notorio for marriages in Italy, US citizens
facts.use_note: CONFLICT on witness numbers: the US Embassy (F-06) says two witnesses; the Italian Consulates in New York and Los Angeles (F-20) say four. Recommend the article say 'two to four witnesses depending on where you swear it: the Italian consulates in New York and Los Angeles ask for four' and tell readers to confirm with their consulate. Page undated.

facts.claim: The Italian Consulate General in Los Angeles lists: US passport; an Atto Notorio sworn in the US at the consulate by the applicant and four witnesses (over 18, unrelated to the couple); a sworn declaration before a US Consulate in Italy; evidence of termination of previous marriages translated into Italian with an Apostille from the secretary of state where issued. Some cities also require the birth certificate, translated and apostilled. To apply, email the application form, passport copies, witnesses' photo IDs and supporting copies to notarile.losangeles@esteri.it.
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia a Los Angeles, US citizens wishing to marry in Italy
facts.use_note: The LA page says the birth certificate is needed only if the city asks, while the NY page lists a long-form apostilled birth certificate as required. Advise readers to bring one (it is cheap insurance) and confirm with the comune. Page undated.

facts.claim: The Italian Consulate General in San Francisco issues the Atto Notorio on the same day as the appointment; it is a declaration by the US spouse(s) before the Italian Consul supported by two witnesses for each spouse, and it is valid for 90 days, so the marriage must take place within 90 days of issue. The consulate advises first asking the comune whether an apostilled, translated birth certificate is required, and bringing it to the appointment so the consulate can certify the translation. Then obtain the Dichiarazione Giurata in Italy and take everything to the comune's Ufficio Matrimoni.
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia a San Francisco, Foreign (Non-EU) Citizens Marrying in Italy
facts.use_note: Read via LLM extraction, not full text, so medium. Resolves the witness conflict in F-19: 'two witnesses per spouse' means four for a couple where both are American, consistent with New York and Los Angeles. Validity: San Francisco says 90 days, New York says 'within three months' of the marriage: same window. This is tighter than the six-month rule (F-11), so the Atto Notorio is the LAST US-side step, inside 90 days of the wedding.

facts.claim: The Italian Consulate General in New York serves residents of New York State, Connecticut, the New Jersey counties of Bergen, Hudson, Morris, Passaic, Sussex, Union, Warren, Essex, Middlesex, Monmouth, Hunterdon, Mercer and Somerset, and Bermuda.
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia a New York, Consular Network
facts.use_note: A Brooklyn couple uses the New York consulate (690 Park Avenue). Other NJ counties belong to another consulate (likely Philadelphia; not verified).

facts.claim: The Italian Consulate General in Los Angeles covers Southern California plus Arizona, Nevada and New Mexico (honorary consulates in Phoenix, San Diego, Las Vegas and Santa Fe). Northern California residents are served by the Consulate General in San Francisco.
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia a Los Angeles, Consular Network
facts.use_note: LLM extraction only; the exact California county split was not read, and the San Francisco page extraction also listed Nevada, which conflicts. Article should say 'Southern California residents generally use Los Angeles, Northern California residents San Francisco; check your consulate's jurisdiction page' and not list counties. Wedded Advisor to confirm.

facts.claim: Italian consular fee for an Atto Notorio (Art. 26, 'Atti notarili diversi dai precedenti'): EUR 28.00, charged in the US as USD 32.30 from 1 October to 31 December 2026, at the official quarterly exchange rate of EUR 1.00 = USD 1.1516. Certification of a translation's conformity (Art. 72A) is EUR 13.00 (USD 15.00) per page. Fees change quarterly. The New York consulate accepts payment only by money order (no cash, cards or personal checks).
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia a Los Angeles, Estratto Tabella Diritti Consolari, 1 Oct to 31 Dec 2026
facts.use_note: The New York page says the Atto Notorio fees are under art. 25 and 26 and payment rules are at https://consnewyork.esteri.it/it/servizi-consolari-e-visti/servizi-per-il-cittadino-italiano/tariffe-consolari/ . Whether the fee is charged once per couple or per spouse is not stated: write 'about USD 32 per Atto Notorio (Q4 2026)'. Use EUR 1 = USD 1.1516 (Italian MFA consular rate for Q4 2026, valid from 1 Oct 2026) for ALL EUR to USD conversions in the article, with 'at the Italian consular rate for Oct to Dec 2026'.

facts.claim: The US has no governmental document or authority that certifies a citizen is free to marry; US diplomatic and consular officers are not permitted to perform marriages; marriages legally performed and valid abroad are in general legally valid in the United States, and questions on validity go to the attorney general of the state where the couple lives.
facts.source_name: U.S. Department of State, Foreign Affairs Manual 7 FAM 1450 Marriage of U.S. Citizens Abroad
facts.use_note: Explains WHY Americans swear a Dichiarazione Giurata instead of getting a 'Nulla Osta certificate'. Also supports the US recognition answer with F-26.

facts.claim: A foreign marriage that is valid in the country where it is performed is automatically valid in the US. An Italian marriage certificate is sufficient proof and is considered valid once legalized with an Apostille, obtained from the Legalization Office of the Prefettura with jurisdiction over the place of marriage. The Embassy suggests requesting a copy of the certificate from the town hall and getting the Apostille before leaving Italy.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy?
facts.use_note: 'Before leaving Italy' tip is from the district pages ('once married, obtain the Apostille') and the NY Italian consulate page. No US registration step is described on any official page read; say 'there is no US registry to record it in' only with F-25 support, i.e. no US authority issues or registers it.

facts.claim: Apostille fees: New York State Department of State USD 10 per document. For a New York City birth certificate: order a certified copy from the NYC Health Department with a Letter of Exemplification, have the signature verified by the New York County Clerk, then send it to the NYS Department of State with the USD 10 fee. California Secretary of State: USD 20 per Apostille, plus a USD 6 special handling fee for each different public official's signature; in person in Sacramento or Los Angeles, or by mail.
facts.source_name: New York State Department of State, Apostille or Certificate of Authentication; NYC311; California Secretary of State
facts.use_note: NYC steps from https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01020 ; California from https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/request-apostille and https://www.sos.ca.gov/notary/apostille-faqs (search snippets plus extraction, not full text, hence medium). The NYC chain has three stops, which is why couples should start in month 6, not week 6.

facts.claim: US federal documents (for example a naturalization certificate copy) are apostilled by the US Department of State Office of Authentications: submit Form DS-4194 with a USD 20 nonrefundable fee per document. Mail requests take about 5 weeks or more; walk-in drop-off is processed within about 7 business days; same-day appointments are for immediate family emergencies only.
facts.source_name: U.S. Department of State, Request Authentication Services
facts.use_note: Read via extraction. Whether a naturalized couple needs a naturalization document for the comune is not stated by any Italian source read: put in needs.

facts.claim: Translations for use in Italy: the Italian Consulate General in Los Angeles does not translate documents but legalizes translations already made; the translation does not have to be by an official translator, only done professionally. Send the original (an Apostille is mandatory for vital records), the translation, a money order or cashier's check for the Art. 72A fee per sheet (EUR 13, USD 15.00 in Q4 2026) and a prepaid return envelope (UPS not accepted).
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia a Los Angeles, Traduzione e legalizzazione dei documenti
facts.use_note: Resolves the brief's Peach Perfect question: an official sworn translator is not required by the Italian consulates in the US, but the translation should be professional and is then certified by the Italian consulate (Miami and San Francisco pages also say the consulate certifies translations; New York says divorce decrees need a professional translation with a Certificate of Accuracy plus an Apostille). Comuni may also accept translations sworn in Italy (asseverazione) but no official source for that was read: see N-06. Article line: 'have a professional translate, then have your Italian consulate certify it, unless your comune tells you otherwise'.

facts.claim: The Italian Consulate General in New York asks for a long-form certified birth certificate (with both parents' names) apostilled by the state where the birth took place and accurately translated into Italian, and for previously married applicants a final divorce decree or death certificate with Apostille; the divorce decree must be professionally translated, certified with a 'Certificate of Accuracy', and apostilled by the state where the translation was certified. The consulate suggests getting a copy of the marriage certificate from the City Hall and having it apostilled at the local Prefettura before leaving Italy.
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia a New York, Atto Notorio for marriages in Italy, US citizens
facts.use_note: The same page describes banns of eight days plus four, usually waived for non-residents; this is older wording than the US Embassy's (F-09). Use the Embassy version for banns.

facts.claim: A New York State marriage license is valid for 60 calendar days, beginning the day after it is issued (180 days for active military), and there is a 24-hour waiting period before the ceremony unless a judge waives it.
facts.source_name: New York State Department of Health, Information on Getting Married in New York State
facts.use_note: For the 'legal at home first' route. Military detail from https://www.cityclerk.nyc.gov/content/marriage-license . Read from search snippets of both official pages.

facts.claim: A Los Angeles County marriage license is valid for 90 days.
facts.source_name: Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk, Recording Your Marriage Certificate
facts.use_note: Read from the official page snippet. Pair with F-31 to show validity windows vary by state and county; tell readers to check their county clerk.

facts.claim: To change a name with Social Security after marriage, request a replacement Social Security card (often online via my Social Security, otherwise by appointment at a local office) with proof of the name change such as a marriage certificate; originals or certified copies are required, not photocopies. There is no fee. Foreign-language documents need a certified translation.
facts.source_name: U.S. Social Security Administration, Change name with Social Security
facts.use_note: Online start and 'marriage certificate is ideal' also on the SSA blog of 22 Oct 2026: https://www.ssa.gov/blog/en/posts/2026-10-22.html . Page read via LLM extraction, so the translation and no-fee points are medium; Wedded Advisor or writer to spot-check. Social Security first, then passport and driver's license, is the usual order (driver's license step: state DMV rules vary, not researched).

facts.claim: US passport name change after marriage: if less than one year since the passport was issued, mail Form DS-5504 with the passport, an original or certified marriage certificate and one photo, with no fee (USD 60 for expedited service). If more than one year, renew by mail (DS-82) with a certified copy of the name change document if eligible, or apply in person. A certified English translation is required for foreign-language documents.
facts.source_name: U.S. Department of State, Change or Correct a Passport
facts.use_note: Read via LLM extraction plus search snippet. Renewal fees not quoted; link the page. Practical note: the Italian certificate is in Italian, so budget for a certified English translation for SSA and the passport (see N-11).

facts.claim: For US federal taxes, filing status generally depends on marital status on the last day of the year, so a couple married on any date in a year is generally treated as married for that whole tax year.
facts.source_name: Internal Revenue Service, Filing status; Essential tax tips for marriage status changes
facts.use_note: One line only, no advice. Also https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/essential-tax-tips-for-marriage-status-changes .

facts.claim: Getting married is a qualifying life event: couples may qualify for a Special Enrollment Period on HealthCare.gov if they married in the past 60 days, and usually have 60 days around the event to enroll.
facts.source_name: HealthCare.gov, Getting health coverage outside Open Enrollment
facts.use_note: One line. Employer plans have their own rules; say 'check your employer plan's window too' without numbers.

facts.claim: Italy regulates civil unions between people of the same sex under Law 76/2016 (with Decree 144/2016); Italian consulates forward foreign same-sex marriage or civil union certificates to the comune for registration in the civil unions registry. Italian law provides civil unions, not marriage, for same-sex couples.
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia a Boston, Civil Unions
facts.use_note: For the same-sex FAQ: one line plus link to our dedicated article. The page does not set out the procedure for two foreign nationals entering a civil union in Italy; do not describe it (N-05).

facts.claim: Italian comuni issue multilingual civil status extracts (estratti plurilingue) under the Vienna Convention of 8 September 1976; when requested for marriage-related use the purpose should be specified.
facts.source_name: Comune di Parma, Estratti plurilingue
facts.use_note: Read from search snippets only (Parma and Montalto di Castro comune pages). The US is not shown as a party to the 1976 Convention and no US source says a multilingual extract avoids translation for SSA or passports. Article may say 'ask the comune for a multilingual extract as well as the standard certificate, then apostille it at the Prefettura' only after Wedded Advisor confirmation (N-11).

facts.claim: A religious ceremony performed by a Roman Catholic priest is legally valid and needs no separate civil ceremony, as the priest registers the marriage with the civil authorities; the Church also requires baptismal and confirmation certificates. A ceremony by non-Catholic clergy requires a civil ceremony beforehand to make the marriage legal.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy?
facts.use_note: Comparison table in H2 2.

facts.claim: For English-language marriages at the Vatican, couples contact the parish priest of Saint Patrick's Church; Vatican marriages are registered by Vatican City civil authorities, and because the Vatican is a separate state the Dichiarazione Giurata is required but does not need legalization by an Italian Prefettura.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy?
facts.use_note: Optional one sentence. Do not link stpatricksamericanrome.org unless approved.

facts.claim: Completing all procedures may take several days; timing varies with how many marriages the civil authorities are handling, and waiting lists are common in popular towns and in May, June and September.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy?
facts.use_note: No official source gives a fixed number of days in Italy before the wedding. Sample schedule must be labelled as an illustration (N-07).

facts.claim: No residency requirement for marrying in Italy is stated on the US Embassy page; the documents and declarations listed (F-02 to F-10) are the requirements for US citizens, and banns are waived or shortened when neither party is an Italian citizen or resident.
facts.source_name: U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Italy, Getting Married in Italy?
facts.use_note: Inference from absence plus the banns waiver for non-residents. Phrase as 'You do not need to live in Italy: the US Embassy's requirements for Americans include no residency period', not as a quoted rule.

facts.claim: Exchange rate for all conversions in this article: EUR 1.00 = USD 1.1516, the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular rate (tasso di ragguaglio) for 1 October to 31 December 2026.
facts.source_name: Consolato Generale d'Italia a Los Angeles, Estratto Tabella Diritti Consolari (Q4 2026)
facts.use_note: Official, dated, and the rate Italian consulates in the US actually charge at. Write conversions as 'about USD X (at EUR 1 = USD 1.15, Oct 2026)'. Market rates differ slightly; this is an approximation.

legal.summary: Marriage law is national, but each comune interprets it and sets the final document list and timing. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
Documents: US passport, birth certificate, proof prior marriages ended; 300-day waiver rule (F-03). Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
Dichiarazione Giurata sworn at a US post in Italy by appointment; it functions as the Nulla Osta. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
Dichiarazione legalized at a Prefettura in the same consular district, EUR 16 stamp per document. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.

Atto Notorio sworn by non-relative witnesses before an Italian consul in the US or a court in Italy. Witness count conflicts (two per US Embassy, four per Italian consulates in NY and LA, two per spouse per San Francisco): see F-19, F-21. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
Atto Notorio in an Italian court: interpreter if needed, stamps EUR 42.62 standard (4 to 10 days) or EUR 63.86 urgent. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
Declaration of Intention to Marry at the comune's Ufficio Matrimoni, with interpreter if needed. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
Banns waived or shortened (one day to a week) when neither party is Italian or resident. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
Civil ceremony by mayor or deputy, two adult witnesses with photo ID, witness cannot be interpreter. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
Non-EU public documents valid six months from issue. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
US documents need an Apostille from the issuing state's secretary of state (federal documents: US Department of State) and an Italian translation. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
US consular districts by region (Rome, Florence, Milan, Naples). Medium confidence: source page dated 2013 but consistent with current district pages. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
Prefettura pairings per district, including Salerno for the Amalfi Coast and the Venice and Genoa agency rule. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
Atto Notorio at the Italian Consulate in New York: four unrelated witnesses in person, within three months of the wedding, booked via email and Prenot@mi. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
Atto Notorio at the Italian Consulate in Los Angeles: applicant plus four unrelated witnesses; apply by email. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
Atto Notorio issued same day, two witnesses per spouse, valid 90 days. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
No US document or authority certifies freedom to marry; US consuls cannot perform marriages; valid foreign marriages generally valid in the US. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
Italian marriage valid in Italy is automatically valid in the US; Italian certificate with Prefettura Apostille is proof. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
Translations: professional translation certified by the Italian consulate; official sworn translator not required by the LA consulate; comune may differ. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.
